subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Lion as King
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Lion as King.

hook.text: Lions guard entrances across cultures: Chinese stone lions, Egyptian sphinxes, and British coat of arms.

buildup.text: The male lion's mane resembles a crown. Its roar dominates. Cultures that never saw lions still used them.

discovery.text: In the Bible, Judah is a lion. Christ is the Lion of Judah. In Buddhism, the lion represents the Buddha's voice.

twist.text: Female lions do the hunting. The 'king' symbol is built on the male who mostly sleeps. Myth got the biology wrong.

climax.text: The lion's symbolic power has nothing to do with real lions. It's about what humans project onto a mane and a roar.

punchline.text: The mane is the myth. The roar seals it.

quiz.question: What biological fact contradicts the lion-as-king myth?
options: Female lions do most of the hunting
